outcome_verbatim: Participants were classified as achieving sustained employment if they maintained full-time work/study or part-time work for 12 consecutive months in the third year of follow-up.
source_locator: Table 1, 'Sustained employment' row, Schizophrenia (n = 374) column, p. 3; construct defined in Methods 2.2 Measures, p. 2 and in Table 1 footnote b, p. 3
conflict_note: CONSTRUCT: the source contradicts itself about what sustained employment counts. Methods 2.2 (p. 2) defines it as 'maintained full-time work/study or part-time work for 12 consecutive months in the third year of follow-up', i.e. full-time STUDY counts. Table 1 footnote b (p. 3) defines the same variable as 'maintaining full-time or part-time work for the last 12 months of the 3-year follow-up' and Table 2 footnote e (p. 3) as 'maintained full-time or part-time employment in the last 12 months'; both omit study. The numerator is therefore either a paid-work-or-education composite (Methods) or any paid work (footnotes), which are different constructs in different outcome families. Not resolvable from the report. DENOMINATOR: Table 1 heads the schizophrenia column n = 374 and prints sustained employment as '111 (30.0)'. 111/374 = 29.7%, and NO integer numerator over 374 gives 30.0% (112/374 = 29.9%, 113/374 = 30.2%), so the printed percentage cannot have been computed on 374. 111/370 = 30.0% exactly, and the printed chi-square of 4.6 for this comparison reproduces at 370 (4.63) but not at 374 (4.85 uncorrected, 4.14 with continuity correction); every other percentage in the same column reproduces exactly on 374 (38/374 = 10.2%, 43/374 = 11.5%, 76/374 = 20.3%, 162/374 = 43.3%) and their chi-squares also reproduce on 374. Four schizophrenia patients therefore appear to be missing from the employment denominator, and the report never says so.
notes: n_outcome_observed LEFT BLANK. 374 is the number of schizophrenia patients who completed 3-year follow-up (recorded in n_assessed), not a stated employment denominator, and the report's own arithmetic shows the employment denominator was not 374. 370 is recorded in reported_percentage_base only: it is the unique integer base consistent with the printed 30.0%, corroborated by the printed chi-square, but the report never prints it, so it is a reporting base and not an observed denominator (extraction prompt rule 7). NOT DERIVED ACROSS ARMS: 111 + 21 = 132 of 420 would be a whole-sample figure the paper never prints, its two components sit on different arms and different denominators, and one of those denominators is contradicted, so it is not written. ASCERTAINMENT: coded period_prevalence with a 12-month window (months 24 to 36) because the measure is defined over a stated window rather than at the timepoint; note that it is stricter than the vocabulary's period prevalence, requiring employment MAINTAINED throughout the 12 months rather than at any point in it, so it is not comparable with an 'employed during the past year' register measure either. HORIZON: 36 months falls in no prespecified band (t24m closes at 30 months, t60m opens at 48), so this result cannot enter any landmark horizon even if the conflicts are resolved. Moderators left blank: the baseline characteristics table is supplementary Table S1, which is cited but not present in the PDF.
